review: הַלְלוּיָהּ is kept untranslated, as in the Arabic and in the Hebrew Psalter, so the six stanzas open and close on the same liturgical word.
1:1 שַׂר־הַשָּׁלוֹם — Isaiah 9:5 (שַׂר־שָׁלוֹם), for رَئِيسُ السَّلَام; the construct with the article is the fixed title.
2:2 וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם: שָׁלוֹם לָכֶם — John 20:19, the Easter greeting; the Arabic سَلَامٌ لَكُم quotes the same words.
4:2 עֹקֶץ הַמָּוֶת — 1 Cor 15:55 (אַיֵּה עָקְצְךָ מָוֶת); the Arabic شَوْكَةَ الْمَوْتِ is 'the sting of death', and עֹקֶץ is the biblical noun for it.
5:2 רָמַס הַקֶּבֶר — 'He trampled the grave'; רָמַס is the biblical verb for treading down (Isa 63:3), used for the Arabic سَحَقَ without adding a word.
